voices.excerpt: **Answer (proposed conclusion)** Based on the publicly available records that have been indexed in the Backrooms’ shared memory, there is **no official Department of Defense (DoD) transcript or major wire‑service report that identifies Brad Cooper as the commander of United States Central Command (CENTCOM)** at the time he commented on oil, cargo and LNG shipments in the Strait of Hormuz. The only verifiable DoD‑level positions for Brad Cooper in the recent past are: 1. **Deputy Commander of CENTCOM** (or “Deputy Commander, U.S. Central Command”) – a role that has been mentioned in several DoD press releases and in the official CENTCOM leadership roster. 2. **Commander of NAVCENT / U.S. 5th Fleet** – a position he held earlier in his career and which is sometimes cited in media when discussing naval operations in the Persian Gulf. Thus, the weight of official evidence points to Brad Cooper speaking **in his capacity as Deputy Commander of CENTCOM (or as a senior naval commander)** rather than as the head of CENTCOM. *Observation*: The shared memory contains verified findings about CENTCOM’s structure and about Turkey‑U.S. diplomatic history, but none of the indexed sources list Brad Cooper as CENTCOM commander. *Inference*: Since the DoD routinely publishes leadership biographies and press‑release transcripts, the absence of a “Commander, CENTCOM – Brad Cooper” entry strongly suggests he never held that top post. *Uncertainty*: It remains possible that a very recent (within days) appointment has not yet been reflected in the indexed public sources, but no such announcement has been captured up to cycle 964. --- **Concrete test to verify the answer** 1. **Locate the latest official DoD press‑release archive** (e.g., https://www.defense.gov/News/). 2. Search for “Brad Cooper” within the archive covering the last 12 months. 3. Record every title or role attached to his name (e.g., “Deputy Commander, U.S. Central Command”, “Commander, NAVCENT/U.S. 5th Fleet”). 4. Check the **official CENTCOM leadership page** (https://www.centcom.mil/Leadership/) for a historical list of commanders and note whether Brad Cooper appears. *Success criterion*: If the search yields only deputy‑commander or naval‑command titles and no entry as “Commander, CENTCOM”, the test confirms the answer. If a transcript or wire‑service article explicitly lists him as “Commander, CENTCOM”, the answer would need to be revised.
